editorial:
Imagine waking up in the middle of the night to your daughter screaming that a stranger just broke into her room. That is exactly how things kick off here, and it quickly turns the whole neighborhood upside down. You get to see how fast people jump to conclusions, especially when they start blaming the local convenience store owner just because he is an outsider. While the town is fighting over whether the girl is lying or not, you also follow Paul. He is a middle-aged dad who is just trying to fix his broken relationship with his daughter before she grows up and leaves him behind for good. It is a quiet, heavy movie that feels very real.

What really hits home is the acting, as the characters feel like people you actually know. The pacing is a bit slow, so you will need some patience, but the emotional payoff is worth it. If you enjoy stories about family secrets and small-town drama, you should definitely give this a shot. It is the kind of film that stays on your mind long after the credits roll.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up by showing that the truth is more complicated than a simple crime. You find out that the girl's claims were more about her own internal struggles and family tension than an actual intruder. The story ends with Paul finally reaching a point of understanding with his daughter. They do not fix everything instantly, but they find a way to communicate again, leaving you with a feeling of hope for their future.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves character studies and emotional family stories.
